name: Bulk Send Customer Welcome Email
script:
"""
Bulk "Welcome" Email Sender for Customer Portal Users
======================================================

Loops through a list of Customers, emails each linked Portal User a
welcome message (from an existing Email Template) with a working
password-reset link.

USAGE
-----
Save as a Server Script (Script Type: API). Call from client:

    frappe.call({
        method: "send_customer_welcome_emails",
        args: { customers: JSON.stringify(["SUP-0001", "SUP-0002"]) }
    })

REQUIRES
--------
- Email Template named EMAIL_TEMPLATE_NAME, with Subject + body filled in.
- Customer's standard "Portal Users" child table (field: user -> User).
- Optional: "Customer Welcome Email Log" doctype (customer, status,
  remarks, sent_by, sent_on) for an audit trail. Skipped if missing.

NOTES
-----
- json is a preset global in the Server Script sandbox, not imported.
- reset_password_url comes from User.reset_password() itself, not a
  hand-rolled random key — frappe.utils.random_string / frappe.generate_hash
  are both blocked in this sandbox (Frappe deliberately excludes
  token-generation functions from Server Scripts).
- No permission check on this script (removed on request). Any user who
  can call this API can trigger real emails + password-reset regen for
  any customer. To restrict it, add as the first line:
      if not frappe.has_permission("Customer", "write"):
          frappe.throw("Not permitted.", frappe.PermissionError)
  (frappe.get_roles() and frappe.only_for() are NOT available in this
  sandbox — both raise AttributeError at runtime.)
"""

# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
# Config
# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
EMAIL_TEMPLATE_NAME = "Portal Welcome Email - FORTUNA IMPEX PVT LTD"
COMPANY_NAME = "Fortuna Impex Pvt Ltd"
LOG_DOCTYPE = "Customer Welcome Email Log"

# Public portal URL, if different from the site's own URL (proxy/custom
# domain). Leave "" to use frappe.utils.get_url() instead.
PORTAL_URL = ""
#PORTAL_URL = "http://dts.connectcloud365.com:57194"


# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
# Read & validate input
# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
customers = frappe.form_dict.get("customers")

if isinstance(customers, str):
    try:
        customers = json.loads(customers)
    except Exception:
        frappe.throw("`customers` must be a valid JSON array of Customer IDs.")

if not customers or not isinstance(customers, list):
    frappe.throw("Please provide at least one Customer ID in `customers`.")


# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
# Load the Email Template once, fail fast if it's missing/incomplete
# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
if not frappe.db.exists("Email Template", EMAIL_TEMPLATE_NAME):
    frappe.throw(f"Email Template '{EMAIL_TEMPLATE_NAME}' does not exist.")

template = frappe.get_doc("Email Template", EMAIL_TEMPLATE_NAME)
# .get() avoids AttributeError if response_html isn't a real field (getattr() is blocked in this sandbox).
email_body = template.get("response_html") or template.response or ""

if not template.subject or not email_body:
    frappe.throw("The Email Template must have both a Subject and a Response (body).")

customer_meta = frappe.get_meta("Customer")
has_log_doctype = bool(frappe.db.exists("DocType", LOG_DOCTYPE))

results = []  # per-customer / per-user outcome, returned to the caller


# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
# Helpers
# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
def log_attempt(customer, status, remarks):
    """Best-effort audit log row — never lets a logging error break the run."""
    if not has_log_doctype:
        return
    try:
        frappe.get_doc({
            "doctype": LOG_DOCTYPE,
            "customer": customer,
            "status": status,
            "remarks": remarks,
            "sent_by": frappe.session.user,
            "sent_on": frappe.utils.now_datetime(),
        }).insert(ignore_permissions=True)
    except Exception as e:
        frappe.log_error(
            title="Welcome Email Log Failed",
            message=f"Could not write log for {customer}: {e}",
        )


def get_portal_base_url():
    """PORTAL_URL if defined and set, else the site's own URL. No trailing slash."""
    try:
        url = (PORTAL_URL or "").strip()
    except NameError:
        url = ""
    
    return (url or frappe.utils.get_url()).rstrip("/") 


def get_portal_login_url():
    """Plain login page — NOT a magic reset link. Frappe blocks all
    password/token-generation calls inside Server Scripts by design (same
    reason get_roles/only_for/generate_hash/random_string are blocked:
    Server Scripts are creatable by any System Manager, so anything
    account-takeover-adjacent is off-limits, on any object, everywhere).
    Users click "Forgot Password" on this page themselves instead."""
    return f"{get_portal_base_url()}/login"
	
# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
# 6. Helper — generate a WORKING password-reset link for one portal user.
# Mirrors what frappe.core.doctype.user.user.User.reset_password() does
# internally: the key is random and stored as-is (not hashed), because
# /update-password matches it as-is.
# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
def build_reset_password_url(user_email):
    reset_key = frappe.utils.generate_hash()

    frappe.db.set_value(
        "User",
        user_email,
        {
            "reset_password_key": frappe.utils.sha256_hash(reset_key),
            "last_reset_password_key_generated_on": frappe.utils.now_datetime(),
        },
    )

    return f"{get_portal_base_url()}/update-password?key={reset_key}"
	


# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
# Main loop — one Customer, then one Portal User, at a time.
# Failures are caught at the narrowest scope so one bad row never stops
# the rest of the batch.
# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
for customer_name in customers:

    if not customer_name:
        results.append({
            "customer": customer_name,
            "status": "skipped",
            "error": "Empty Customer ID",
            "message": "Skipped — empty Customer ID in request",
        })
        continue

    if not frappe.db.exists("Customer", customer_name):
        log_attempt(customer_name, "Failed", "Customer not found")
        results.append({
            "customer": customer_name,
            "status": "failed",
            "error": "Customer not found",
            "message": f"Failed — Customer '{customer_name}' does not exist",
        })
        continue

    customer = frappe.get_doc("Customer", customer_name)

    # Skip already-welcomed customers (needs custom_is_welcome_email_sent field).
    # if customer.get("custom_is_welcome_email_sent"):
    #     results.append({"customer": customer_name, "status": "skipped - already sent"})
    #     continue

    # De-duplicate in case a user is listed twice in Portal Users.
    portal_user_emails = list({
        row.user.strip()
        for row in (customer.get("portal_users") or [])
        if row.user and row.user.strip()
    })

    if not portal_user_emails:
        log_attempt(customer_name, "Skipped", "No portal user linked")
        results.append({
            "customer": customer_name,
            "status": "skipped - no portal user",
            "message": f"{customer.customer_name} — no portal user linked, nothing sent",
        })
        continue

    sent_count = 0

    for portal_user_email in portal_user_emails:

        if not frappe.db.exists("User", portal_user_email):
            log_attempt(customer_name, "Failed", f"User not found: {portal_user_email}")
            results.append({
                "customer": customer_name,
                "portal_user": portal_user_email,
                "status": "failed",
                "error": "User not found",
                "message": f"Failed for {customer.customer_name} ({portal_user_email}) — user not found",
            })
            continue

        try:
            user_doc = frappe.get_doc("User", portal_user_email)

            context = {
                "doc": customer,
                "party_type": "Customer",
                "portal_url": get_portal_base_url(),
                "portal_email": portal_user_email,
                "company": COMPANY_NAME,
                "reset_password_url": build_reset_password_url(portal_user_email),
                "first_name": user_doc.first_name or "",
                "full_name": user_doc.full_name or user_doc.first_name or "",
            }

            frappe.sendmail(
                recipients=[portal_user_email],
                subject=frappe.render_template(template.subject, context),
                message=frappe.render_template(email_body, context),
                now=True,
            )

            log_attempt(customer_name, "Sent", f"Bulk Welcome email sent to {portal_user_email}")
            sent_count += 1
            results.append({
                "customer": customer_name,
                "portal_user": portal_user_email,
                "status": "sent",
                "message": f"Email sent to {customer.customer_name} ({portal_user_email})",
            })

        except Exception as e:
            frappe.log_error(
                title="Bulk Welcome Email Failed",
                message=f"Customer: {customer_name}\nPortal user: {portal_user_email}\n\n{e}",
            )
            log_attempt(customer_name, "Failed", f"Failed to send to {portal_user_email}. See Error Log.")
            results.append({
                "customer": customer_name,
                "portal_user": portal_user_email,
                "status": "failed",
                "error": "Check Error Log for details",
                "message": f"Failed to send to {customer.customer_name} ({portal_user_email})",
            })

    # Stamp the customer once, only if at least one email actually sent.
    if sent_count:
        if customer_meta.has_field("custom_is_welcome_email_sent"):
            customer.db_set("custom_is_welcome_email_sent", 1)
        if customer_meta.has_field("custom_welcome_email_sent_on"):
            customer.db_set("custom_welcome_email_sent_on", frappe.utils.now_datetime())
        if customer_meta.has_field("custom_welcome_email_sent_by"):
            customer.db_set("custom_welcome_email_sent_by", frappe.session.user)

frappe.response["message"] = results

name: Send Customer Welcome Email on First Sales Order
script:
# =============================================================================
# Customer Portal Welcome Email
# =============================================================================
#
# Sends a one-time welcome email to a Customer's portal user(s), triggered on
# their FIRST submitted Sales Order.
#
# Trigger:   Sales Order -> on_submit
#
# IMPORTANT (Frappe Server Script / safe_exec constraints):
#   - This runs inside safe_exec. Do NOT use frappe.get_traceback() - it is
#     not exposed in that sandbox.
#   - safe_exec executes this script with SEPARATE globals and locals
#     dictionaries, and it also removes access to `globals()`, `locals()`,
#     `eval()`, `exec()` etc. entirely (confirmed: calling globals() here
#     raises "NameError: name 'globals' is not defined"). That combination
#     means:
#       * Any name bound by a top-level statement in this script (constants,
#         `doc`, and top-level `def`s) lives ONLY in the script's locals.
#       * A function's internal name lookups go through its own
#         __globals__, which does NOT include that locals dict.
#       * There is no supported way to bridge the two via introspection.
#     Net effect: a top-level helper function calling another top-level
#     helper function - or referencing `doc` - fails at runtime with
#     "NameError: name 'x' is not defined", even though the code reads
#     correctly and only `frappe` (pre-injected into true globals by the
#     sandbox) resolves normally from inside such functions.
#   - The fix used throughout this script: ALL config, helpers, and flow
#     logic are nested INSIDE ONE outer function, `run_welcome_email(doc)`.
#     Nested functions resolve each other and `doc` via ordinary Python
#     closures (lexical/enclosing scope), which is unaffected by the
#     globals/locals split - no introspection required. Only the single
#     top-level call `run_welcome_email(doc)` touches the script's true
#     top-level namespace, and that works the same way `doc.docstatus`
#     already did safely elsewhere in this script.
#
# Guarantee:
#   A failure anywhere in this automation must NEVER fail the Sales Order
#   submission. The whole flow is wrapped in one try/except so the worst
#   outcome is a missed/failed email, recorded in Error Log and/or Customer
#   Welcome Email Log - never a blocked submit.
#
# "First submitted Sales Order" logic:
#   This intentionally replaces the older custom_is_welcome_email_sent flag
#   approach. We count the customer's other submitted Sales Orders
#   (excluding the current one, since this script runs after submission):
#
#       0 other submitted SOs  -> this is the first SO -> attempt the email
#       1+ other submitted SOs -> do nothing
#
#   Email Template body field:
#     This site stores the template body in `response_html`, not the
#     standard `response` field, so load_valid_email_template() reads
#     `response_html` first and falls back to `response` if that's blank.
#
#   Known limitations of this approach (by design, not fixed here):
#     - If the customer's true first SO is later cancelled, the next SO will
#       look like "the first" again and will re-trigger the welcome email and
#       re-stamp the audit fields.
#     - If the first email attempt fails, later Sales Orders will NOT retry
#       automatically. Use the separate bulk "Send Welcome Email" API script
#       to resend manually.
#     - A row lock (see is_first_submitted_order) narrows, but does not fully
#       eliminate, a race condition where two Sales Orders for the same new
#       customer are submitted at nearly the same instant.
#
# =============================================================================


def run_welcome_email(doc):
    """
    Single entry point for the whole automation. Everything - config,
    helpers, and the main flow - is nested here so it all resolves through
    normal closures instead of safe_exec's split globals/locals namespaces.
    """

    # -------------------------------------------------------------------
    # CONFIG
    # -------------------------------------------------------------------

    EMAIL_TEMPLATE_NAME = "Portal Welcome Email - FORTUNA IMPEX PVT LTD"

    COMPANY_NAME = "Fortuna Impex Pvt Ltd"

    LOG_DOCTYPE = "Customer Welcome Email Log"

    SENT_FLAG_FIELD = "custom_is_welcome_email_sent"
    SENT_ON_FIELD = "custom_welcome_email_sent_on"
    SENT_BY_FIELD = "custom_welcome_email_sent_by"

    # Leave empty to use the site's own URL via frappe.utils.get_url().
    # Example: PORTAL_URL = "http://dts.connectcloud365.com:57194"
    PORTAL_URL = ""

    # If True, skip the automation for Sales Orders whose `company` does not
    # match COMPANY_NAME. Off by default to preserve original behaviour;
    # turn on if this script is ever attached in a multi-company setup where
    # only Fortuna Impex orders should trigger this specific template.
    ENFORCE_COMPANY_MATCH = False

    # -------------------------------------------------------------------
    # HELPERS - shared utilities
    # -------------------------------------------------------------------

    def get_portal_base_url(portal_url):
        """
        Resolve the portal base URL: the configured override, or the
        site's own URL as a fallback. Trailing slash stripped for clean
        concatenation.
        """
        url = (portal_url or "").strip()

        if not url:
            url = frappe.utils.get_url()

        return url.rstrip("/")

    def build_reset_password_url(user_email, portal_url):
        """
        Generate a password-reset link for a portal User.

        The raw reset key is embedded in the returned URL; only its
        SHA-256 hash is persisted on the User record, matching Frappe's
        own reset-password convention.
        """
        reset_key = frappe.utils.generate_hash()

        frappe.db.set_value(
            "User",
            user_email,
            {
                "reset_password_key": frappe.utils.sha256_hash(reset_key),
                "last_reset_password_key_generated_on": frappe.utils.now_datetime(),
            },
        )

        base_url = get_portal_base_url(portal_url)
        return f"{base_url}/update-password?key={reset_key}"

    def log_attempt(customer_name, status, remarks):
        """
        Best-effort audit log write to the Customer Welcome Email Log
        doctype.

        Silently no-ops if the log doctype doesn't exist (e.g. not
        installed on this site), and swallows any insert failure into
        Error Log - logging must never be a second point of failure for
        the Sales Order submission.
        """
        if not frappe.db.exists("DocType", LOG_DOCTYPE):
            return

        try:
            frappe.get_doc(
                {
                    "doctype": LOG_DOCTYPE,
                    "customer": customer_name,
                    "status": status,
                    "remarks": remarks,
                    "sent_by": frappe.session.user,
                    "sent_on": frappe.utils.now_datetime(),
                }
            ).insert(ignore_permissions=True)

        except Exception as e:
            # frappe.get_traceback() is unavailable in Server Script safe_exec.
            frappe.log_error(
                title="Customer Welcome Email Log Failed",
                message=f"Could not write welcome email log for {customer_name}: {e}",
            )

    # -------------------------------------------------------------------
    # HELPERS - welcome email flow
    # -------------------------------------------------------------------

    def is_first_submitted_order(customer_name, current_so_name):
        """
        True if current_so_name is the customer's only submitted Sales
        Order.

        Takes a short row lock on the Customer record first so that two
        Sales Orders for the same brand-new customer submitted nearly
        simultaneously serialize against each other, rather than both
        reading "zero prior orders" and both sending a welcome email.
        This reduces but does not fully close that race window (actual
        behaviour still depends on the database's transaction isolation
        level).
        """
        frappe.db.sql("SELECT name FROM `tabCustomer` WHERE name = %s FOR UPDATE", customer_name)

        other_submitted = frappe.db.count(
            "Sales Order",
            {
                "customer": customer_name,
                "docstatus": 1,
                "name": ["!=", current_so_name],
            },
        )
        return other_submitted == 0

    def get_email_body(template):
        """
        Resolve the template's body text.

        This site stores the body in `response_html` rather than the
        standard `response` field, so that's checked first, falling back
        to `response`. `.get()` is used instead of attribute access so a
        missing field returns None rather than raising.
        """
        return template.get("response_html") or template.get("response") or ""

    def load_valid_email_template(customer_name):
        """
        Load and validate the configured Email Template.

        Returns the template doc on success, or None (after logging) if
        it's missing or has no usable Subject/body. Returns a single
        value only (never a tuple) - this sandbox's safe_exec does not
        support tuple-unpacking assignment (no `_unpack_sequence_` guard
        available), so every call site here uses plain single-name
        assignment instead.
        """
        if not frappe.db.exists("Email Template", EMAIL_TEMPLATE_NAME):
            msg = f"Email Template '{EMAIL_TEMPLATE_NAME}' does not exist."
            frappe.log_error(title="Customer Welcome Email - Template Missing", message=msg)
            log_attempt(customer_name, "Failed", msg)
            return None

        template = frappe.get_doc("Email Template", EMAIL_TEMPLATE_NAME)
        email_body = get_email_body(template)

        if not template.subject or not email_body:
            msg = f"Email Template '{EMAIL_TEMPLATE_NAME}' must have both Subject and a Response/Response HTML body."
            frappe.log_error(title="Customer Welcome Email - Template Incomplete", message=msg)
            log_attempt(customer_name, "Failed", msg)
            return None

        return template

    def get_valid_portal_emails(customer):
        """
        Return a de-duplicated list of non-blank portal user emails linked
        to the Customer's `portal_users` child table. Logs and returns []
        if there are no usable rows.
        """
        portal_user_rows = customer.get("portal_users") or []

        if not portal_user_rows:
            log_attempt(customer.name, "Skipped", "No portal user linked - nothing to email")
            return []

        emails = []
        for row in portal_user_rows:
            email = (row.user or "").strip()
            if email and email not in emails:
                emails.append(email)

        if not emails:
            log_attempt(customer.name, "Skipped", "No valid portal user email found")

        return emails

    def send_welcome_email(portal_user_email, customer, template, email_body):
        """
        Send the welcome email to a single portal user and log the
        outcome.

        `email_body` is the already-resolved template body (see
        load_valid_email_template - it may come from `response_html` or
        `response`), passed in explicitly rather than re-derived here.

        Returns True on success, False on any failure (missing User,
        template render error, SMTP failure, etc). This function must
        never raise - a single recipient's failure must not stop the loop
        over other recipients, let alone the Sales Order submission.
        """
        if not frappe.db.exists("User", portal_user_email):
            log_attempt(customer.name, "Failed", f"User not found: {portal_user_email}")
            return False

        try:
            user_doc = frappe.get_doc("User", portal_user_email)
            portal_base_url = get_portal_base_url(PORTAL_URL)
            reset_password_url = build_reset_password_url(portal_user_email, PORTAL_URL)

            context = {
                "doc": customer,
                "customer": customer,
                "party_type": "Customer",
                "portal_url": portal_base_url,
                "portal_email": portal_user_email,
                "company": doc.company or COMPANY_NAME,
                "reset_password_url": reset_password_url,
                "first_name": user_doc.first_name or "",
                "full_name": user_doc.full_name or user_doc.first_name or "",
            }

            frappe.sendmail(
                recipients=[portal_user_email],
                subject=frappe.render_template(template.subject, context),
                message=frappe.render_template(email_body, context),
                now=True,
            )

            log_attempt(
                customer.name,
                "Sent",
                f"Welcome Email sent to {portal_user_email}, on First Sales Order {doc.name}",
            )
            return True

        except Exception as e:
            # frappe.get_traceback() is unavailable in Server Script safe_exec.
            frappe.log_error(
                title=f"Customer Welcome Email Failed - {customer.name} - {portal_user_email}",
                message=(
                    f"Customer: {customer.name}\n"
                    f"Portal User: {portal_user_email}\n"
                    f"Sales Order: {doc.name}\n"
                    f"Error: {e}"
                ),
            )
            log_attempt(
                customer.name,
                "Failed",
                f"Welcome email could not be sent to {portal_user_email}. Check Error Log for details.",
            )
            return False

    def stamp_customer_audit_fields(customer, customer_meta):
        """
        Stamp optional audit fields on the Customer, once at least one
        email in this run has actually been sent. Each field is stamped
        only if it exists on the doctype, so this is safe on sites
        without the custom fields.
        """
        if customer_meta.has_field(SENT_FLAG_FIELD):
            customer.db_set(SENT_FLAG_FIELD, 1)

        if customer_meta.has_field(SENT_ON_FIELD):
            customer.db_set(SENT_ON_FIELD, frappe.utils.now_datetime())

        if customer_meta.has_field(SENT_BY_FIELD):
            customer.db_set(SENT_BY_FIELD, frappe.session.user)

    # -------------------------------------------------------------------
    # MAIN FLOW
    # -------------------------------------------------------------------
    # Structured as early returns so each precondition (submitted, correct
    # company, first order, valid template, valid recipients) is checked
    # once and short-circuits cleanly. The whole block is wrapped in one
    # try/except so ANY unexpected failure - including ones upstream of the
    # per-recipient send loop - is caught and logged here, rather than
    # propagating up and failing the Sales Order submission itself.
    # -------------------------------------------------------------------

    try:
        if doc.docstatus != 1:
            return

        if ENFORCE_COMPANY_MATCH and doc.company and doc.company != COMPANY_NAME:
            return

        if not is_first_submitted_order(doc.customer, doc.name):
            # Not this customer's first submitted Sales Order - by design,
            # we do nothing (see module header for reasoning/limitations).
            return

        customer = frappe.get_doc("Customer", doc.customer)
        customer_meta = frappe.get_meta("Customer")

        template = load_valid_email_template(doc.customer)
        if not template:
            return
        email_body = get_email_body(template)

        portal_emails = get_valid_portal_emails(customer)
        if not portal_emails:
            return

        sent_count = 0
        for portal_user_email in portal_emails:
            if send_welcome_email(portal_user_email, customer, template, email_body):
                sent_count += 1

        # Only stamp audit fields if at least one email actually went out.
        if sent_count:
            stamp_customer_audit_fields(customer, customer_meta)

    except Exception as e:
        frappe.log_error(
            title="Customer Welcome Email - Unexpected Failure",
            message=f"Customer: {doc.customer}\nSales Order: {doc.name}\nError: {e}",
        )
        log_attempt(doc.customer, "Failed", f"Unexpected error: {e}")


# Entry point. This call is true top-level script code, so `doc` (injected
# by Frappe for this doc event) resolves exactly the way it always has
# elsewhere in this script - no closures or globals bridging needed here,
# only inside the function above.
run_welcome_email(doc)

name: Supplier Welcome
script:
# =============================================================================
# Supplier Onboarding - Auto-create Supplier/Portal User + Contact + Welcome Email
# =============================================================================
#
# Trigger:   Supplier Onboarding -> on_update
#
# Behaviour:
#   - Runs whenever the onboarding doc is saved while docstatus == 1
#     (submitted/approved). Because on_update fires on EVERY save, not just
#     the transition into docstatus 1, every step below must be safe to run
#     repeatedly on the same document.
#   - Creates the Supplier (once) and links it back to this doc.
#   - Creates (or updates) a standard Contact for the supplier, linked to
#     the Supplier via the Dynamic Link "links" child table, with email,
#     mobile, and designation populated - once.
#   - Creates a portal User for the supplier's contact email (once).
#   - Ensures the User has the "Supplier" role and is linked via the
#     Supplier's portal_users table.
#   - Sends the configured welcome email - but only the FIRST time this
#     supplier is fully onboarded (see "Idempotency" below). This was a
#     real bug in the previous version: with no send-guard, the email went
#     out again on every subsequent edit to an already-onboarded record.
#   - Writes a best-effort audit log to LOG_DOCTYPE.
#
# Idempotency:
#   - Supplier creation:   guarded by doc.get("supplier") - safe to re-run.
#   - Contact creation:    guarded by an existing-link check against the
#                          Supplier via Dynamic Link - safe to re-run. If a
#                          Contact already exists for this Supplier, it is
#                          reused and its email/phone rows are topped up
#                          rather than duplicated.
#   - User creation:       guarded by frappe.db.exists("User", email) - safe.
#   - Role / portal link:  guarded by an existing-row check - safe.
#   - Welcome email:       ** GUARD CURRENTLY DISABLED **. Intended design:
#                          check LOG_DOCTYPE for a prior "Sent" entry for
#                          this supplier before sending, so repeated
#                          on_update calls stop re-sending once it has gone
#                          out successfully once. That check
#                          (has_already_sent_welcome_email) and its call
#                          site are currently commented out below on
#                          request - while disabled, the welcome email
#                          WILL be resent on every future save of an
#                          already-onboarded record. Re-enable both
#                          commented blocks before running this against
#                          real approvals. A prior "Failed" entry was
#                          never meant to block a retry either way - the
#                          next save attempt tries again, unlike the Sales
#                          Order welcome email script (which requires a
#                          manual bulk resend). This is intentional: unlike
#                          Sales Order submission, on_update fires
#                          naturally on future edits here, giving it a
#                          built-in retry path.
#
# Known limitation (not changed here - flagging instead of silently
# altering existing validation behaviour):
#   - get_portal_email() calls frappe.throw() if no contact email is set.
#     Because on_update re-runs this on every save, a submitted onboarding
#     record with no email will keep throwing on EVERY future edit to that
#     document (even edits unrelated to the portal email), until an email
#     is added. If that's not the desired behaviour, consider logging and
#     returning early instead of throwing, or only enforcing this at the
#     specific transition into docstatus == 1 rather than on every update.
#   - The same applies to Contact creation below: it runs right after
#     get_portal_email(), so it inherits that same hard-stop behaviour if
#     no email is present. This mirrors the existing design rather than
#     introducing a new failure mode.
#
# IMPORTANT (Frappe Server Script / safe_exec constraints - confirmed
# empirically while debugging the sibling Sales Order welcome email script):
#   - Do NOT use frappe.get_traceback() - not exposed in safe_exec.
#   - safe_exec runs this script with separate globals/locals dicts, AND
#     removes access to globals()/locals()/eval()/exec() entirely. A
#     top-level function calling another top-level function (or referencing
#     `doc`) fails with "NameError: name 'x' is not defined", and there is
#     no way to bridge the namespaces via introspection.
#     Fix used here: every helper and the whole flow are nested INSIDE ONE
#     outer function, run_supplier_onboarding(doc). Nested functions
#     resolve each other and `doc` via ordinary Python closures, which is
#     unaffected by the globals/locals split. Only `frappe` is looked up
#     via true globals (confirmed pre-injected by the sandbox), and only
#     the single top-level call `run_supplier_onboarding(doc)` touches the
#     script's true top-level namespace.
#   - No identifier anywhere may start with "_" (RestrictedPython rejects
#     it, e.g. "invalid variable name because it starts with '_'").
#   - No tuple-unpacking assignment (e.g. `a, b = f()`) - this sandbox has
#     no `_unpack_sequence_` guard available, so it fails with
#     "NameError: name '_unpack_sequence_' is not defined". Every helper
#     below returns a single value; multi-value results are obtained via
#     separate single-purpose calls instead.
#
# =============================================================================


def run_supplier_onboarding(doc):
    """
    Single entry point. See module header for the full design notes.
    """

    # -------------------------------------------------------------------
    # CONFIG
    # -------------------------------------------------------------------

    EMAIL_TEMPLATE_NAME = "Portal Welcome Email - FORTUNA IMPEX PVT LTD"
    COMPANY_NAME = "Fortuna Impex Pvt Ltd"
    LOG_DOCTYPE = "Supplier Welcome Email Log"

    # Leave empty to use the site's own URL via frappe.utils.get_url().
    # Example: PORTAL_URL = "http://dts.connectcloud365.com:57194"
    PORTAL_URL = ""

    # -------------------------------------------------------------------
    # HELPERS - shared utilities
    # -------------------------------------------------------------------

    def get_portal_base_url(portal_url):
        """
        Resolve the portal base URL: the configured override, or the
        site's own URL as a fallback. Trailing slash stripped for clean
        concatenation.
        """
        url = (portal_url or "").strip()

        if not url:
            url = frappe.utils.get_url()

        return url.rstrip("/")

    def build_reset_password_url(user_email, portal_url):
        """
        Generate a password-reset link for a portal User.

        The raw reset key is embedded in the returned URL; only its
        SHA-256 hash is persisted on the User record.
        """
        reset_key = frappe.utils.generate_hash()

        frappe.db.set_value(
            "User",
            user_email,
            {
                "reset_password_key": frappe.utils.sha256_hash(reset_key),
                "last_reset_password_key_generated_on": frappe.utils.now_datetime(),
            },
        )

        base_url = get_portal_base_url(portal_url)
        return f"{base_url}/update-password?key={reset_key}"

    def log_attempt(supplier_name, status, remarks):
        """
        Best-effort audit log write. Logging must never cause the
        Supplier Onboarding save itself to fail, so any insert failure
        here is swallowed into Error Log rather than raised.
        """
        if not frappe.db.exists("DocType", LOG_DOCTYPE):
            return

        try:
            frappe.get_doc(
                {
                    "doctype": LOG_DOCTYPE,
                    "supplier": supplier_name,
                    "status": status,
                    "remarks": remarks,
                    "sent_by": frappe.session.user,
                    "sent_on": frappe.utils.now_datetime(),
                }
            ).insert(ignore_permissions=True)

        except Exception as e:
            frappe.log_error(
                title="Supplier Welcome Email Log Failed",
                message=f"Could not write log for {supplier_name}: {e}",
            )

    # DISABLED (commented out on request): this guard checks LOG_DOCTYPE
    # for a prior "Sent" entry so the welcome email isn't resent every time
    # on_update fires on an already-onboarded record. With it disabled, the
    # welcome email WILL be sent again on every future save of a submitted
    # Supplier Onboarding doc - this is the bug the function exists to fix
    # (see module header "Idempotency" section). Re-enable before this runs
    # against real approvals.
    #
    # def has_already_sent_welcome_email(supplier_name):
    #     """
    #     True if LOG_DOCTYPE already has a "Sent" entry for this supplier.
    #
    #     This is the fix for the main bug in the previous version: without
    #     this check, on_update re-firing on every future edit to an
    #     already-onboarded record would resend the welcome email every
    #     single time.
    #     """
    #     if not frappe.db.exists("DocType", LOG_DOCTYPE):
    #         return False
    #
    #     return bool(
    #         frappe.db.exists(LOG_DOCTYPE, {"supplier": supplier_name, "status": "Sent"})
    #     )

    def get_email_body(template):
        """
        Resolve the template's body text. This site stores the body in
        `response_html` rather than the standard `response` field, so
        that's checked first, falling back to `response`.
        """
        return template.get("response_html") or template.get("response") or ""

    def load_valid_email_template(supplier_name):
        """
        Load and validate the configured Email Template. Returns the
        template doc, or None (after logging) if it's missing or has no
        usable Subject/body.
        """
        if not frappe.db.exists("Email Template", EMAIL_TEMPLATE_NAME):
            msg = f"Email Template '{EMAIL_TEMPLATE_NAME}' does not exist."
            frappe.log_error(title="Supplier Welcome Email - Template Missing", message=msg)
            log_attempt(supplier_name, "Failed", msg)
            return None

        template = frappe.get_doc("Email Template", EMAIL_TEMPLATE_NAME)
        email_body = get_email_body(template)

        if not template.subject or not email_body:
            msg = f"Email Template '{EMAIL_TEMPLATE_NAME}' must have both Subject and a Response/Response HTML body."
            frappe.log_error(title="Supplier Welcome Email - Template Incomplete", message=msg)
            log_attempt(supplier_name, "Failed", msg)
            return None

        return template

    # -------------------------------------------------------------------
    # HELPERS - onboarding steps (each idempotent - safe to re-run)
    # -------------------------------------------------------------------

    def ensure_supplier():
        """
        Load the linked Supplier if one already exists on this onboarding
        doc, otherwise create it and link it back. Field mappings below
        assume standard Supplier fields plus india_compliance's tax_id for
        GSTIN - adjust if your Supplier doctype differs.
        """
        if doc.get("supplier"):
            return frappe.get_doc("Supplier", doc.supplier)

        supplier = frappe.new_doc("Supplier")
        supplier.supplier_name = doc.get("supplier_name") or doc.name

        supplier.supplier_group = doc.get("supplier_group") or ""
        supplier.supplier_type = doc.get("supplier_type") or "Company"
        supplier.address_line1 = doc.get("address_line1") or ""
        supplier.city = doc.get("city") or ""
        supplier.state = doc.get("state") or ""
        supplier.country = doc.get("country") or ""
        supplier.pincode = doc.get("pincode") or ""
        supplier.tax_id = doc.get("gstin") or ""
        supplier.pan = doc.get("pan") or ""
        supplier.custom_status = "Approved"

        supplier.insert(ignore_permissions=True)

        # Link Supplier back to the onboarding document.
        doc.db_set("supplier", supplier.name)

        return supplier

    def get_portal_email():
        """
        Resolve and normalize the supplier's portal contact email.

        Raises via frappe.throw if missing - this is an intentional hard
        requirement (unlike the welcome email itself, which is best-effort
        - see module header for the "re-throws on every future edit" edge
        case this causes if the email is never provided).
        """
        email = doc.get("email") or doc.get("email")

        if not email:
            frappe.throw("Supplier portal email is required before approval.")

        return email.strip().lower()

    def find_linked_contact(supplier_name):
        """
        Look up an existing Contact already linked to this Supplier via
        the standard Dynamic Link "links" child table. Returns the Contact
        name (string) or None. This is the idempotency guard for Contact
        creation: a Supplier should only ever get one auto-created Contact
        from this script, regardless of how many times on_update fires.
        """
        linked = frappe.db.get_all(
            "Dynamic Link",
            filters={
                "link_doctype": "Supplier",
                "link_name": supplier_name,
                "parenttype": "Contact",
            },
            fields=["parent"],
            limit=1,
        )

        if linked:
            return linked[0].parent

        return None

    def ensure_contact_email_row(contact, portal_user_email):
        """
        Add portal_user_email to the Contact's email_ids child table if it
        isn't already present, marking it primary when it's the first row.
        """
        already_present = False

        for row in contact.get("email_ids") or []:
            if row.email_id == portal_user_email:
                already_present = True
                break

        if not already_present:
            is_primary = 0 if contact.get("email_ids") else 1
            contact.append("email_ids", {"email_id": portal_user_email, "is_primary": is_primary})

    def ensure_contact_phone_row(contact, mobile):
        """
        Add the mobile number to the Contact's phone_nos child table if
        it isn't already present, marking it primary mobile when it's the
        first row.

        This site has a custom mandatory field on the "Contact Phone"
        child table, custom_mobile_number (label "Mobile Number"),
        separate from the standard "phone" field - Frappe's own mandatory
        check enforces it even though it isn't part of the standard
        doctype. Both fields are set to the same value here so the row
        validates regardless of which one the site's forms/reports read.

        Trims whitespace before checking truthiness - a whitespace-only
        value is not a usable phone number, and passing it straight
        through used to reach these mandatory fields as an
        effectively-blank string, raising a MandatoryError on save/insert.
        """
        mobile = (mobile or "").strip()

        if not mobile:
            return

        already_present = False

        for row in contact.get("phone_nos") or []:
            if (row.phone or "").strip() == mobile:
                already_present = True
                if not (row.get("custom_mobile_number") or "").strip():
                    row.custom_mobile_number = mobile
                break

        if not already_present:
            is_primary_mobile = 0 if contact.get("phone_nos") else 1
            contact.append(
                "phone_nos",
                {
                    "phone": mobile,
                    "is_primary_mobile_no": is_primary_mobile,
                    "custom_mobile_number": mobile,
                },
            )

    def remove_blank_phone_rows(contact):
        """
        Drop any phone_nos rows with a blank/whitespace-only phone value,
        and backfill custom_mobile_number on any kept row that's missing
        it. Defensive cleanup for rows that predate the strip() fix and
        the custom_mobile_number fix above (or were added by hand
        elsewhere) - both "phone" and this site's custom
        custom_mobile_number field on Contact Phone are mandatory, so a
        row missing either one fails save() on every future onboarding
        update, not just the one that created it.
        """
        keep_rows = []

        for row in contact.get("phone_nos") or []:
            phone = (row.phone or "").strip()

            if not phone:
                continue

            if not (row.get("custom_mobile_number") or "").strip():
                row.custom_mobile_number = phone

            keep_rows.append(row)

        contact.set("phone_nos", keep_rows)

    def ensure_supplier_contact(supplier, portal_user_email):
        """
        Create (once) a standard Contact for this Supplier, or reuse and
        top up an existing one. Idempotent via find_linked_contact() above
        - safe to re-run on every on_update.

        Returns the Contact doc.
        """
        existing_contact_name = find_linked_contact(supplier.name)

        if existing_contact_name:
            contact = frappe.get_doc("Contact", existing_contact_name)
            contact.designation = doc.get("designation") or contact.get("designation") or ""
            remove_blank_phone_rows(contact)
            ensure_contact_email_row(contact, portal_user_email)
            ensure_contact_phone_row(contact, doc.get("mobile"))
            contact.save(ignore_permissions=True)
            return contact

        contact = frappe.new_doc("Contact")
        contact.first_name = doc.get("first_name") or supplier.supplier_name
        contact.last_name = doc.get("last_name") or ""
        contact.designation = doc.get("designation") or ""
        contact.append("links", {"link_doctype": "Supplier", "link_name": supplier.name})
        ensure_contact_email_row(contact, portal_user_email)
        ensure_contact_phone_row(contact, doc.get("mobile"))
        contact.insert(ignore_permissions=True)

        return contact

    def ensure_portal_user(portal_user_email):
        """
        Load the portal User for this email if it already exists,
        otherwise create it. `designation` is set defensively via
        attribute assignment - if the User doctype on this site has no
        such field, Frappe simply won't persist it, so this is harmless.
        """
        if frappe.db.exists("User", portal_user_email):
            return frappe.get_doc("User", portal_user_email)

        user = frappe.new_doc("User")
        user.email = portal_user_email
        user.first_name = doc.get("first_name") or "Supplier"
        user.last_name = doc.get("last_name") or ""
        user.mobile_no = doc.get("mobile") or ""
        user.designation = doc.get("designation") or ""
        user.enabled = 1
        user.user_type = "Website User"
        user.send_welcome_email = 0
        user.insert(ignore_permissions=True)

        return user

    def ensure_supplier_role(user):
        """Add the "Supplier" role to the portal User if not already present."""
        has_supplier_role = False

        for role in user.get("roles") or []:
            if role.role == "Supplier":
                has_supplier_role = True
                break

        if not has_supplier_role:
            user.append("roles", {"role": "Supplier"})
            user.save(ignore_permissions=True)

    def ensure_portal_link(supplier, portal_user_email):
        """
        Link the portal User into the Supplier's portal_users child table,
        if that field exists on this site's Supplier doctype and the link
        isn't already present.
        """
        supplier_meta = frappe.get_meta("Supplier")

        if not supplier_meta.has_field("portal_users"):
            return

        already_linked = False

        for row in supplier.get("portal_users") or []:
            if row.user == portal_user_email:
                already_linked = True
                break

        if not already_linked:
            supplier.append("portal_users", {"user": portal_user_email})
            supplier.save(ignore_permissions=True)

    def send_welcome_email(supplier, user, portal_user_email, template, email_body):
        """
        Send the welcome email and log the outcome. Must never raise -
        by this point Supplier/User creation has already succeeded, and a
        failure here must not undo or block that (see module header: "Do
        NOT throw here").
        """
        try:
            portal_base_url = get_portal_base_url(PORTAL_URL)
            reset_password_url = build_reset_password_url(portal_user_email, PORTAL_URL)

            context = {
                "doc": doc,
                "supplier": supplier,
                "user": user,
                "party_type": "Supplier",
                "portal_url": portal_base_url,
                "portal_email": portal_user_email,
                "company": COMPANY_NAME,
                "reset_password_url": reset_password_url,
                "first_name": user.first_name or "",
                "full_name": user.full_name or user.first_name or "",
            }

            frappe.sendmail(
                recipients=[portal_user_email],
                subject=frappe.render_template(template.subject, context),
                message=frappe.render_template(email_body, context),
                now=True,
            )

            log_attempt(supplier.name, "Sent", f"Welcome email sent to {portal_user_email}")
            return True

        except Exception as e:
            # frappe.get_traceback() is unavailable in Server Script safe_exec.
            frappe.log_error(
                title=f"Supplier Welcome Email Failed - {supplier.name}",
                message=f"Supplier: {supplier.name}\nPortal User: {portal_user_email}\nError: {e}",
            )
            log_attempt(
                supplier.name,
                "Failed",
                f"Welcome email could not be sent to {portal_user_email}. Check Error Log for details.",
            )
            return False

    # -------------------------------------------------------------------
    # MAIN FLOW
    # -------------------------------------------------------------------
    # Supplier/Contact/User/role/link creation are intentionally left
    # unguarded by a blanket try/except: if any of that core onboarding
    # work fails, the exception should propagate and fail the save,
    # exactly as it did before this refactor - that's a real problem
    # worth surfacing, unlike a welcome-email delivery failure. Only
    # send_welcome_email (above) is self-contained, matching the original
    # "Do NOT throw here" intent for the email step specifically.
    # -------------------------------------------------------------------

    if doc.docstatus != 1:
        return

    supplier = ensure_supplier()
    portal_user_email = get_portal_email()
    ensure_supplier_contact(supplier, portal_user_email)
    user = ensure_portal_user(portal_user_email)

    ensure_supplier_role(user)
    ensure_portal_link(supplier, portal_user_email)

    # DISABLED (commented out on request), along with the function above.
    # See the warning there: without this check, the block below runs -
    # and sends the welcome email - on every future save of this doc.
    #
    # if has_already_sent_welcome_email(supplier.name):
    #     # Already onboarded and welcomed in a previous save - this
    #     # on_update firing again (e.g. an unrelated edit) is a no-op from
    #     # here on.
    #     return

    template = load_valid_email_template(supplier.name)
    if not template:
        return

    email_body = get_email_body(template)
    send_welcome_email(supplier, user, portal_user_email, template, email_body)


# Entry point. True top-level call, so `doc` (injected by Frappe for this
# doc event) resolves normally - no closures or bridging needed here, only
# inside the function above.
run_supplier_onboarding(doc)

"""
Bulk "Welcome" Email Sender for Supplier Portal Users
======================================================

Loops through a list of Suppliers, emails each linked Portal User a
welcome message (from an existing Email Template) with a working
password-reset link.

USAGE
-----
Save as a Server Script (Script Type: API). Call from client:

    frappe.call({
        method: "send_supplier_welcome_emails",
        args: { suppliers: JSON.stringify(["SUP-0001", "SUP-0002"]) }
    })

REQUIRES
--------
- Email Template named EMAIL_TEMPLATE_NAME, with Subject + body filled in.
- Supplier's standard "Portal Users" child table (field: user -> User).
- Optional: "Supplier Welcome Email Log" doctype (supplier, status,
  remarks, sent_by, sent_on) for an audit trail. Skipped if missing.

NOTES
-----
- json is a preset global in the Server Script sandbox, not imported.
- reset_password_url comes from User.reset_password() itself, not a
  hand-rolled random key — frappe.utils.random_string / frappe.generate_hash
  are both blocked in this sandbox (Frappe deliberately excludes
  token-generation functions from Server Scripts).
- No permission check on this script (removed on request). Any user who
  can call this API can trigger real emails + password-reset regen for
  any supplier. To restrict it, add as the first line:
      if not frappe.has_permission("Supplier", "write"):
          frappe.throw("Not permitted.", frappe.PermissionError)
  (frappe.get_roles() and frappe.only_for() are NOT available in this
  sandbox — both raise AttributeError at runtime.)
"""

# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
# Config
# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
EMAIL_TEMPLATE_NAME = "Portal Welcome Email - FORTUNA IMPEX PVT LTD"
COMPANY_NAME = "Fortuna Impex Pvt Ltd"
LOG_DOCTYPE = "Supplier Welcome Email Log"

# Public portal URL, if different from the site's own URL (proxy/custom
# domain). Leave "" to use frappe.utils.get_url() instead.
PORTAL_URL = ""
#PORTAL_URL = "http://dts.connectcloud365.com:57194"


# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
# Read & validate input
# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
suppliers = frappe.form_dict.get("suppliers")

if isinstance(suppliers, str):
    try:
        suppliers = json.loads(suppliers)
    except Exception:
        frappe.throw("`suppliers` must be a valid JSON array of Supplier IDs.")

if not suppliers or not isinstance(suppliers, list):
    frappe.throw("Please provide at least one Supplier ID in `suppliers`.")


# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
# Load the Email Template once, fail fast if it's missing/incomplete
# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
if not frappe.db.exists("Email Template", EMAIL_TEMPLATE_NAME):
    frappe.throw(f"Email Template '{EMAIL_TEMPLATE_NAME}' does not exist.")

template = frappe.get_doc("Email Template", EMAIL_TEMPLATE_NAME)
# .get() avoids AttributeError if response_html isn't a real field (getattr() is blocked in this sandbox).
email_body = template.get("response_html") or template.response or ""

if not template.subject or not email_body:
    frappe.throw("The Email Template must have both a Subject and a Response (body).")

supplier_meta = frappe.get_meta("Supplier")
has_log_doctype = bool(frappe.db.exists("DocType", LOG_DOCTYPE))

results = []  # per-supplier / per-user outcome, returned to the caller


# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
# Helpers
# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
def log_attempt(supplier, status, remarks):
    """Best-effort audit log row — never lets a logging error break the run."""
    if not has_log_doctype:
        return
    try:
        frappe.get_doc({
            "doctype": LOG_DOCTYPE,
            "supplier": supplier,
            "status": status,
            "remarks": remarks,
            "sent_by": frappe.session.user,
            "sent_on": frappe.utils.now_datetime(),
        }).insert(ignore_permissions=True)
    except Exception as e:
        frappe.log_error(
            title="Welcome Email Log Failed",
            message=f"Could not write log for {supplier}: {e}",
        )


def get_portal_base_url():
    """PORTAL_URL if defined and set, else the site's own URL. No trailing slash."""
    try:
        url = (PORTAL_URL or "").strip()
    except NameError:
        url = ""
    
    return (url or frappe.utils.get_url()).rstrip("/")   


def get_portal_login_url():
    """Plain login page — NOT a magic reset link. Frappe blocks all
    password/token-generation calls inside Server Scripts by design (same
    reason get_roles/only_for/generate_hash/random_string are blocked:
    Server Scripts are creatable by any System Manager, so anything
    account-takeover-adjacent is off-limits, on any object, everywhere).
    Users click "Forgot Password" on this page themselves instead."""
    return f"{get_portal_base_url()}/login"
	
# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
# 6. Helper — generate a WORKING password-reset link for one portal user.
# Mirrors what frappe.core.doctype.user.user.User.reset_password() does
# internally: the key is random and stored as-is (not hashed), because
# /update-password matches it as-is.
# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
def build_reset_password_url(user_email):
    reset_key = frappe.utils.generate_hash()

    frappe.db.set_value(
        "User",
        user_email,
        {
            "reset_password_key": frappe.utils.sha256_hash(reset_key),
            "last_reset_password_key_generated_on": frappe.utils.now_datetime(),
        },
    )

    return f"{get_portal_base_url()}/update-password?key={reset_key}"
	


# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
# Main loop — one Supplier, then one Portal User, at a time.
# Failures are caught at the narrowest scope so one bad row never stops
# the rest of the batch.
# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
for supplier_name in suppliers:

    if not supplier_name:
        results.append({
            "supplier": supplier_name,
            "status": "skipped",
            "error": "Empty Supplier ID",
            "message": "Skipped — empty Supplier ID in request",
        })
        continue

    if not frappe.db.exists("Supplier", supplier_name):
        log_attempt(supplier_name, "Failed", "Supplier not found")
        results.append({
            "supplier": supplier_name,
            "status": "failed",
            "error": "Supplier not found",
            "message": f"Failed — Supplier '{supplier_name}' does not exist",
        })
        continue

    supplier = frappe.get_doc("Supplier", supplier_name)

    # Skip already-welcomed suppliers (needs custom_is_welcome_email_sent field).
    # if supplier.get("custom_is_welcome_email_sent"):
    #     results.append({"supplier": supplier_name, "status": "skipped - already sent"})
    #     continue

    # De-duplicate in case a user is listed twice in Portal Users.
    portal_user_emails = list({
        row.user.strip()
        for row in (supplier.get("portal_users") or [])
        if row.user and row.user.strip()
    })

    if not portal_user_emails:
        log_attempt(supplier_name, "Skipped", "No portal user linked")
        results.append({
            "supplier": supplier_name,
            "status": "skipped - no portal user",
            "message": f"{supplier.supplier_name} — no portal user linked, nothing sent",
        })
        continue

    sent_count = 0

    for portal_user_email in portal_user_emails:

        if not frappe.db.exists("User", portal_user_email):
            log_attempt(supplier_name, "Failed", f"User not found: {portal_user_email}")
            results.append({
                "supplier": supplier_name,
                "portal_user": portal_user_email,
                "status": "failed",
                "error": "User not found",
                "message": f"Failed for {supplier.supplier_name} ({portal_user_email}) — user not found",
            })
            continue

        try:
            user_doc = frappe.get_doc("User", portal_user_email)

            context = {
                "doc": supplier,
                "party_type": "Supplier",
                "portal_url": get_portal_base_url(),
                "portal_email": portal_user_email,
                "company": COMPANY_NAME,
                "reset_password_url": build_reset_password_url(portal_user_email),
                "first_name": user_doc.first_name or "",
                "full_name": user_doc.full_name or user_doc.first_name or "",
            }

            frappe.sendmail(
                recipients=[portal_user_email],
                subject=frappe.render_template(template.subject, context),
                message=frappe.render_template(email_body, context),
                now=True,
            )

            log_attempt(supplier_name, "Sent", f"Bulk Welcome email sent to {portal_user_email}")
            sent_count += 1
            results.append({
                "supplier": supplier_name,
                "portal_user": portal_user_email,
                "status": "sent",
                "message": f"Email sent to {supplier.supplier_name} ({portal_user_email})",
            })

        except Exception as e:
            frappe.log_error(
                title="Bulk Welcome Email Failed",
                message=f"Supplier: {supplier_name}\nPortal user: {portal_user_email}\n\n{e}",
            )
            log_attempt(supplier_name, "Failed", f"Failed to send to {portal_user_email}. See Error Log.")
            results.append({
                "supplier": supplier_name,
                "portal_user": portal_user_email,
                "status": "failed",
                "error": "Check Error Log for details",
                "message": f"Failed to send to {supplier.supplier_name} ({portal_user_email})",
            })

    # Stamp the supplier once, only if at least one email actually sent.
    if sent_count:
        if supplier_meta.has_field("custom_is_welcome_email_sent"):
            supplier.db_set("custom_is_welcome_email_sent", 1)
        if supplier_meta.has_field("custom_welcome_email_sent_on"):
            supplier.db_set("custom_welcome_email_sent_on", frappe.utils.now_datetime())
        if supplier_meta.has_field("custom_welcome_email_sent_by"):
            supplier.db_set("custom_welcome_email_sent_by", frappe.session.user)

frappe.response["message"] = results

# Restrict GL Entry visibility for portal users to their own Customer
# and/or Supplier records. Administrator has unrestricted access.

if frappe.session.user != "Administrator":
    # Escape the current session user before embedding it in the SQL query.
    user = frappe.db.escape(frappe.session.user)

    # Allow GL Entries belonging to the Customer linked to this portal user.
    customer_condition = f"""
        (
            `tabGL Entry`.party_type = 'Customer'
            AND `tabGL Entry`.party IN (
                SELECT pu.parent
                FROM `tabPortal User` pu
                WHERE pu.parenttype = 'Customer'
                  AND pu.user = {user}
            )
        )
    """

    # Allow GL Entries belonging to the Supplier linked to this portal user.
    supplier_condition = f"""
        (
            `tabGL Entry`.party_type = 'Supplier'
            AND `tabGL Entry`.party IN (
                SELECT pu.parent
                FROM `tabPortal User` pu
                WHERE pu.parenttype = 'Supplier'
                  AND pu.user = {user}
            )
        )
    """

    # A portal user may be linked to either or both parties.
    # Keep the Customer/Supplier conditions grouped to preserve
    # correct SQL precedence if additional conditions are added later.
    conditions = f"""
        (
            {customer_condition}
            OR
            {supplier_condition}
        )
    """

name: Party Permission Query - Portal Customer & Supplier Access
script:
# Permission Query: restrict Customer/Supplier records to parties linked
# to the logged-in Portal User. Administrator has unrestricted access.

if frappe.session.user != "Administrator":
    # The DocType must be supplied by the calling Permission Query context.
    # Only Customer and Supplier are permitted to prevent arbitrary table access.
    if doctype not in ("Customer", "Supplier"):
        frappe.throw(
            "This permission query supports Customer and Supplier only."
        )

    # Escape the session user before embedding it in the SQL condition.
    user = frappe.db.escape(frappe.session.user)

    # Escape the validated DocType for use as the Portal User parenttype.
    parenttype = frappe.db.escape(doctype)

    # Restrict results to records explicitly linked to the current
    # portal user through the Portal User child table.
    conditions = f"""
        `tab{doctype}`.name IN (
            SELECT pu.parent
            FROM `tabPortal User` pu
            WHERE pu.parenttype = {parenttype}
              AND pu.user = {user}
        )
    """

name: Get Portal Ledger
script:
# API: return GL Entries for the Customer and/or Supplier linked to
# the currently logged-in Portal User.
#
# The portal user determines the allowed party. Client-supplied party
# values are never trusted.
#
# This follows the same Customer/Supplier scoping used by:
# "GL Entry Permission Query - Portal Party Access"

# ----------------------------------------------------------------------
# Validate the current session
# ----------------------------------------------------------------------

if frappe.session.user == "Guest":
    frappe.throw("You must be logged in to view your ledger.")

# Administrator access is intentionally not given special treatment here.
# "My Ledger" is a portal feature and therefore requires a linked
# Customer/Supplier party even if an Administrator calls the endpoint.

# ----------------------------------------------------------------------
# Determine the requested party type
# ----------------------------------------------------------------------

party_type = frappe.form_dict.get("party_type")

if party_type not in ("Customer", "Supplier"):
    frappe.throw("Invalid party type. Customer or Supplier is required.")

# ----------------------------------------------------------------------
# Resolve the portal user's linked party
# ----------------------------------------------------------------------
# The Portal User table is the authoritative relationship between the
# portal account and its Customer/Supplier party.

linked_party = frappe.db.sql(
    """
    SELECT pu.parent AS party
    FROM `tabPortal User` pu
    WHERE pu.parenttype = %s
      AND pu.user = %s
    LIMIT 1
    """,
    (party_type, frappe.session.user),
    as_dict=True,
)

# ----------------------------------------------------------------------
# Validate party ownership
# ----------------------------------------------------------------------
# Do not allow the client to request another Customer/Supplier's ledger.

if not linked_party:
    frappe.throw(
        f"No {party_type} record is linked to your portal account."
    )

party = linked_party[0].party

# ----------------------------------------------------------------------
# Fetch ledger entries
# ----------------------------------------------------------------------
# The party and party_type are server-resolved, so the client cannot
# manipulate the query to access another party's GL Entries.

entries = frappe.db.sql(
    """
    SELECT
        gle.name,
        gle.posting_date,
        gle.account,
        gle.debit,
        gle.credit,
        gle.debit_in_account_currency,
        gle.credit_in_account_currency,
        gle.account_currency,
        gle.voucher_type,
        gle.voucher_no,
        gle.against,
        gle.remarks,
        gle.is_cancelled
    FROM `tabGL Entry` gle
    WHERE gle.party_type = %s
      AND gle.party = %s
      AND gle.is_cancelled = 0
    ORDER BY gle.posting_date DESC, gle.creation DESC
    """,
    (party_type, party),
    as_dict=True,
)

# ----------------------------------------------------------------------
# Return the ledger response
# ----------------------------------------------------------------------
# Include the resolved party information so the Web Form can display
# the correct Customer/Supplier context.

frappe.response["message"] = {
    "party_type": party_type,
    "party": party,
    "entries": entries,
}

name: Get Portal Party
script:
# API: Return the Customer and/or Supplier linked to the currently
# logged-in Portal User, optionally filtered to a single party_type.
#
# Endpoint: /api/method/get_portal_party
# Args:
#   party_type (optional, str) — "Customer" or "Supplier".
#                                 Omit to return both.
#
# Response: list[dict] with keys: party, party_type, party_name
#           Empty list if no match (or user is Guest).

ALLOWED_PARTY_TYPES = ["Customer", "Supplier"]

# Guests never have a Portal User record — skip the query entirely
# rather than relying on the filter to just return nothing.
if frappe.session.user == "Guest":
    frappe.response["message"] = []
else:
    requested_type = frappe.form_dict.get("party_type")

    if requested_type:
        if requested_type not in ALLOWED_PARTY_TYPES:
            frappe.throw(_("Invalid party_type"))
        party_types = [requested_type]
    else:
        party_types = ALLOWED_PARTY_TYPES

    # Resolve every Customer/Supplier this portal user is linked to.
    result = frappe.get_all(
        "Portal User",
        filters={
            "user": frappe.session.user,
            "parenttype": ["in", party_types],
        },
        fields=["parent as party", "parenttype as party_type"],
        order_by="parenttype",
    )

    # Attach a display name (company name) to each row, since portal
    # pages need this for headings/labels, not just the internal ID.
    # Note: one extra query per row — acceptable here since a portal
    # user is realistically linked to at most one or two parties.
    display_name_field = {
        "Customer": "customer_name",
        "Supplier": "supplier_name",
    }
    for row in result:
        row["party_name"] = frappe.db.get_value(
            row["party_type"], row["party"], display_name_field[row["party_type"]]
        )

    # Defense-in-depth: when a specific party_type was requested, verify
    # every returned row actually matches it. Using an explicit check
    # (not `assert`) because assert is a no-op under `python -O`, which
    # some production configs enable — this must always run.
    if requested_type:
        mismatched = [r for r in result if r["party_type"] != requested_type]
        if mismatched:
            frappe.throw(
                _("Internal error: party_type filter mismatch in get_portal_party")
            )

    frappe.response["message"] = result
